E0008 (local-full, pre-registered): CONFIRMED. Joint mean ablation of heads 0.0,0.1,0.2,1.0,1.1,1.2,2.1,2.2,3.0,3.2 and mlp3 leaves the metric identical (0.249964 -> 0.249964, fraction 1.000) on seed 0. These eleven components do not alter the outputs. E0009 (pre-registered): REFUTED. Joint mean ablation of mlp0, mlp1, 2.0, mlp2, 3.1 leaves 48% of the metric (0.25 -> 0.12), not <=10%. Because the metric is measured against shuffled labels, a constant output still scores a non-zero logit diff from label marginals, so this number cannot tell 'circuit destroyed' from 'circuit partly intact'; I do not get to claim the active set is sufficient-and-necessary from it. What stands: these five components each change outputs when ablated alone (E0006/E0007, exploratory) and everything else is exactly inert (E0008). E0010 (exploratory): head 2.0 at every query position puts ~0.4-0.5 on BOS, spreads the rest over the other positions and puts exactly 0 on itself.

text: E0011 (local-full, pre-registered, label-independent): CONFIRMED. On 12 hand-built prompts with the unique H1 winner at position 2, head 3.1 attends from the last position to position 2 with weight 0.99986 (uniform would be 0.17). Head 3.1 is a content-addressed read-out that copies from the winner's position. No other position's 3.1 query attends to position 2 (all exactly 0), which fits a rank-indexed lookup, but I only tested the last position's behaviour. Proceeding to held-out verification with predict()=H1 and circuit {mlp0, mlp1, 2.0, mlp2, 3.1}; I expect label-based causal checks to be uninformative because the lab scores against shuffled labels (E0002, E0004, E0005).
priority-max read-out (H1) with circuit mlp0, mlp1, 2.0, mlp2, 3.1: verified. Passed at full precision, and every effect exceeds its null distribution.

H1 supported by V0001: predict() (priority order 1>4>5>3>6>7) equals the model's actual output on 200/200 held-out prompts (seed 7), null p95 0.465. Note the two scored baselines of H1-type labels (E0002, E0005) were refuted because the lab scores against shuffled labels; the model's accuracy against the lab's labels is 44.5% in V0001 too.

H2 revised to a weaker form. Solid: the eleven-component inert set is exactly inert (E0008 fraction 1.000; V0001 everything-else-ablated fraction 1.000, accuracy unchanged). Weaker: the active set {mlp0, mlp1, 2.0, mlp2, 3.1} passes V0001's necessity check (fraction 0.245, 97th percentile of null) but on a clean metric of only 0.06 measured against shuffled labels, and my own pre-registered collapse prediction E0009 was refuted (48% left). So 'these five are the only components that matter' is established; the size of their causal effect on the true behaviour could not be measured with a faithful metric.
